title: Volcano Islands
blurb: Why does the ground rumble in Indonesia, and what comes out of a volcano? Find out how mountains can breathe fire.

chapters.title: A Mountain with a Fire Inside
chapters.text:
A volcano is a place where hot melted rock comes out of the Earth. Most volcanoes look like mountains, with a bowl-shaped opening at the top called a crater.

To understand a volcano, think about the Earth as an egg. The thin outside is the crust. We live on it. Under the crust is a thick layer called the mantle. The mantle is so hot that some rock in it melts.

Melted rock under the ground is called magma. When magma pushes out of a volcano, we call it lava. Lava is bright orange and very hot. It becomes hard, black rock when it cools down.

chapters.title: Why So Many in Indonesia?
chapters.text:
Indonesia has more than one hundred active volcanoes. That is a lot for one country. Why?

The Earth's crust is not one piece. It is broken into huge slabs called plates. The plates move very slowly all the time. Sometimes one plate slides under another. When this happens, rock goes down into the hot mantle and melts. The new magma rises and finds a way out. This is how many volcanoes are born.

Indonesia sits where several plates meet. It is part of a long curve of volcanoes and earthquakes around the Pacific Ocean. People call this curve the Ring of Fire.

chapters.title: When a Volcano Erupts
chapters.text:
Deep inside a volcano, magma slowly collects in a big space called a magma chamber. The magma holds gas, like the bubbles in a bottle of fizzy drink. As more magma arrives, the pressure grows.

When the pressure is too high, the volcano erupts. Lava may flow down the side. Hot ash and small rocks may shoot into the air. The ash makes a thick grey cloud that can reach the sky and fall far away.

Not every eruption is the same. Some are quiet, with slow rivers of lava. Others are loud and sudden. Scientists called volcanologists watch the mountain with special tools. They measure tiny shakes in the ground and the gas in the air.

chapters.title: Good Things from Fire
chapters.text:
Volcanoes can be dangerous, but they also give people good things. When ash and lava break down over many years, they turn into very rich soil. Plants grow well in this soil because it is full of minerals. That is why farmers on the slopes of volcanoes can grow rice, coffee, vegetables and tea.

Volcanoes also heat water deep in the ground. The hot water comes up as hot springs. People can bathe in them, and some countries use the heat to make electricity.

Many visitors travel to see volcanoes such as Mount Bromo in East Java. They wake up early to watch the sunrise over its crater.

chapters.title: Staying Safe
chapters.text:
People who live near volcanoes learn how to stay safe. Scientists give each volcano an alert level. A low level means the volcano is calm. A high level means an eruption may be near.

When the level is high, officials ask families to leave. This is called evacuation. People take a bag with water, food and important papers. They go to a safe place far from the mountain.

Falling ash is a danger, too. It can hurt eyes and lungs. People wear masks and glasses, and they stay indoors when they can. They listen to the radio and to the officials. Because of good warnings, many lives are saved every year.
